title: rapid-interview-synthesis-sasha-rivera
body:
Quick synthesis (notes to self) - candidate: Marta R. — Senior Runtime Engineer loop (panel A)
Date: 2025-03-10
Interviewer set: Diego (systems), Evelyn (model-serving), me (runtime + reliability)
Session cadence: 90m total, 45m system design, 30m debugging pair, 15m culture/pace

High level impression:
- Very sharp infra instincts; quickly maps a latency/throughput tradeoff space and calls out caching boundaries.
- Strong mental model for KV cache semantics and async batching; used concise analogies ("KV slices like L1/L2 cache tiers") that signaled prior infra work.
- Pairing exercise was competent but a bit defensive under pressure — asked for clarifying assumptions instead of sketching quick fallbacks.
- Communication: clear, pragmatic, but occasionally too terse when explaining rationale to non-experts.

Scorecard (1-5, my quick weights in parentheses)
- Systems fundamentals (30%): 4 — sound reasoning about sharding and cache invalidation, good edge-case thinking.
- Debugging/triage (25%): 3 — reproduces bugs methodically, missed a simpler off-by-one in the KV index until prompted.
- API/contract design (15%): 4 — comfortable defining stable RPC/semantics for rollouts and fallbacks.
- Collaboration & communication (20%): 3 — would benefit from softer signaling when disagreeing, occasionally interrupts.
- Culture/mission fit (10%): 4 — cares about quality and post-deploy incidents; asked about SLO error budgets explicitly.

Strengths (concrete)
- Fast mapping from product requirement (e.g., 50ms p95) to concrete infra levers (batch size heuristics, eager vs lazy KV prefetch).
- Good intuition for quantization/precision tradeoffs when describing memory-constrained nodes.
- Practical experience with rollout strategies: canary -> shadow -> quick rollback automation hooks.

Weaknesses / Risks
- Slight aversion to quick prototypes: prefers robust designs first which could slow early-stage experiments.
- Defensive in pair programming — sometimes stalls when pushed; not a dealbreaker but flag for senior interview dynamics.
- Not much visible experience with policy-level routing or multi-tenant throttling — talked more about single-customer deployments.

Red flags (if any)
- One comment about "we can just avoid messy telemetry" — follow up to ensure they value observability.
- A bit light on cross-team stakeholder storytelling; may need coaching on product-facing comms.

Concrete examples from the session (quote + context)
- On cache eviction: "I prefer deterministic epoch-based eviction because it makes debugging reproducible across nodes." — good rationale, ask for perf implications under bursty load next round.
- Pairing bug: missed modulo boundary when mapping sequence->cache index; corrected after hint; shows methodical recovery but not first-pass catch.

Recommended next steps
- Move to take-home? I lean yes but with tweaks: give a small prototype that emphasizes fast iteration + telemetry (force them to ship a minimal observable change). Purpose: validate prototype-first comfort and observability mindset.
- Suggested interview-ask: include a 30m conversation with SRE/observability owner to probe telemetry priorities and incident runbook experience.
- If promoted to on-site, include a stakeholder-design exercise (15m) to see product communication.

Draft phrasing for panel passback (short)
- "Marta shows strong runtime and cache design instincts and would be an asset for productionizing low-latency model serving. Recommend next step: take-home prototype focused on shipping & observability; add an SRE shadow for signal on telemetry/incident practice."

Open follow-ups/questions for calibrations
- Ask Diego if he wants a deeper probe into modulus/offset bug pattern as a sign of code style and testing rigor.
- Evelyn to confirm: did candidate show any prior multi-tenant routing/quotas experience? I noted mostly single-tenant anecdotes.

Personal notes to self (hygiene)
- When writing the take-home, make sure instructions explicitly require metrics to be emitted (latency histogram + error counter), and include a short rubric for reviewers.
- Keep an eye on "too-defensive" pattern during future loops; recommended coaching prompt: ask candidate to sketch a quick fallback before deep-diving.

Anchors/refs cited in convo:
- Quick links: JIRA INF-4321 (rollout infra spike), GH PR #2987 (batching experiment), Confluence:ramps-2025 (KV eviction notes)

Raw timeline snippets (for record):
- 00:00-05:00 intro/past projects and quick sanity check
- 05:00-50:00 system design — sharding, cache tiers, rollout semantics
- 50:00-80:00 pair debug — bug reproduction, fix, test heuristics
- 80:00-90:00 culture / SLO conversation

Tagging: leave this in draft — plan to re-edit after Diego/Evelyn micro-huddle (today).

-- Sasha
